\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قسمت} (qismat)}{قسمت (qismat)}]{\ur{قسمت} (qismat) — luck; fortune}

\label{lesson:UR-C532-qismat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a good name, then the Urdu for to be kept up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قسمت}}
\textbf{\ur{قسمت}} — \emph{qismat} — \textquotedblleft{}luck; fortune\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{قسمت} \ur{اچھی} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{میچ} \ur{جیتیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar qismat achchhī huī to ham maich jīteṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If our luck is good, we will win the match.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قسمت}} (\emph{qismat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qisma}, \textquotedblleft{}a share, a portion\textquotedblright{}: the share life deals one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qismat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qismat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar qismat achchhī huī to ham maich jīteṅ ge.} — If our luck is good, we will win the match.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a good name, then the Urdu for to be kept up, then say \emph{qismat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{قسمت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Luck; fortune\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تقدیر} (taqdīr)}{تقدیر (taqdīr)}]{\ur{تقدیر} (taqdīr) — destiny}

\label{lesson:UR-C532-taqdir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be kept up, then the Urdu for luck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تقدیر}}
\textbf{\ur{تقدیر}} — \emph{taqdīr} — \textquotedblleft{}destiny\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تقدیر} \ur{نے} \ur{ساتھ} \ur{دیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{ضرور} \ur{ملیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar taqdīr ne sāth diyā to ham zarūr mileṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If destiny is on our side, we will surely meet.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تقدیر}} (\emph{taqdīr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taqdīr}, \textquotedblleft{}measuring out, decreeing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be kept up, then the Urdu for luck, then say \emph{taqdīr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لاٹری} (lāṭrī)}{لاٹری (lāṭrī)}]{\ur{لاٹری} (lāṭrī) — a lottery}

\label{lesson:UR-C532-latri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for luck, then the Urdu for destiny.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لاٹری}}
\textbf{\ur{لاٹری}} — \emph{lāṭrī} — \textquotedblleft{}a lottery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میری} \ur{لاٹری} \ur{نکلی} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{نیا} \ur{گھر} \ur{خریدوں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar merī lāṭrī niklī to maiṅ nayā ghar kharīdūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I win the lottery, I'll buy a new house.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لاٹری}} (\emph{lāṭrī}) is borrowed from English \emph{lottery}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قرعہ} (qurā)}{قرعہ (qurā)}]{\ur{قرعہ} (qurā) — a draw (of lots)}

\label{lesson:UR-C532-qura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for destiny, then the Urdu for a lottery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قرعہ}}
\textbf{\ur{قرعہ}} — \emph{qurā} — \textquotedblleft{}a draw (of lots)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{قرعے} \ur{میں} \ur{میرا} \ur{نام} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{جاؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar qure meṅ merā nām āyā to maiṅ jāūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If my name comes up in the draw, I'll go.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قرعہ}} (\emph{qurā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qurʿa}, \textquotedblleft{}a lot drawn to decide something\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹاس} (ṭās)}{ٹاس (ṭās)}]{\ur{ٹاس} (ṭās) — a toss (of a coin)}

\label{lesson:UR-C532-tas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a lottery, then the Urdu for a draw (of lots).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹاس}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹاس}} — \emph{ṭās} — \textquotedblleft{}a toss (of a coin)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{ٹاس} \ur{جیتا} \ur{تو} \ur{پہلے} \ur{ہم} \ur{کھیلیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ham ne ṭās jītā to pehle ham kheleṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we win the toss, we will play first.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹاس}} (\emph{ṭās}) is borrowed from English \emph{toss}.
\end{cousinweb}
